title: Who owns result-job completion?
intro: Current nominal completion, acquisition failure limits and direct native entry, alongside the still-unselected regrouping. Boxes denote in-process responsibilities, not packages or deployment containers. Graph views start at the dark Start here node; sequences start at their first message. The textual source inventory defines stopping states A0–A15. Source-admitted counterexamples have not been runtime-tested; association is separate from complete settlement.

discussion.title: Association can transfer; complete settlement is unsupported
discussion.status: Source observation complete; no target or migration selected
discussion.summary: The inventory exposes consumed cancellation lost on a no-ending error, unchecked worker reap, destructor-only partial cleanup and failed-exec terminal recovery. Direct native calls retain host signal changes. One fresh source reviewer corroborated the first two and native restoration limits. A scope/funding agreement must precede repair or a reopened comparison; the book agreement stays later. No product code or behavioural campaign was run.

diagrams.title: Publication, ending and cleanup join before return
diagrams.caption: Nominal current front path when the runner returns its own Ended. Selection is shown without protocol internals; worker wait-error admission is a separate limit. Start events and appearance polls are omitted. Cleanup diagnostics and cancellation precedence apply to supplied observations. No-ending failures are covered by the acquisition view; this is not all-interleaving or runtime preservation evidence.

diagrams.title: Acquisition and no-ending failure limits
diagrams.caption: A0–A15 refer to the textual source inventory in docs/result-job-source-evidence.md. This compact view aggregates stopping branches: early preparation refuses directly; selection failure explicitly removes the prepared workspace; partial allocator cleanup remains local. Solid arrows show control/outcomes, not ownership proof. Amber nodes mark source limits; no repair or alternative is selected.

diagrams.title: Child entry state does not restore the host
diagrams.caption: Current runner changes and caller obligations, not a new native API. Solid arrows are call/lifetime order; the dotted edge compares CLI enabling points with native obligations. A process-lifetime supervisor can explicitly accept persistent dispositions; a returning host needs restoration. Neither arrangement is selected. Terminal recovery and syscall success still need the named runtime checks.
